drops.line: The opener. Provision without panic. The drop about what comes first.
drops.why: Matthew 6 is the chapter about untangling worry from want. The set wears the answer on the chest: seek first, and the rest follows the walk.

briefing.mission: Get the order right. Kingdom first, then watch worry lose its job.

points.p: The chapter names the closet itself: pray with the door shut, seen only by the Father. Everything this brand hangs on starts in that room.
You can't serve God and money. A garment that hangs in a store and still says it is the whole tension of the drop: own things without being owned.
Provision without panic. The birds don't stockpile and the lilies out-dress a king. The argument against worry is the Father's track record.
The order of operations on the back of the set: kingdom first, righteousness first, and 'all these things' get added, not chased.

questions: What actually comes first in your week? Check the calendar, not the intentions.
Where does worry currently do your deciding for you?
What would 'seek first' change about tomorrow morning, concretely?
briefing.prayer: Father, order me. Put first in me what You put first, and quiet what worry keeps loud. I'll seek the Kingdom. You handle the rest. Amen.

drops.line: The black set. A city on a hill can't be hidden. Neither can this.
drops.why: Matthew 5 names who the wearer already is: salt that keeps its taste, light that isn't for hiding. The darkest colorway carries the brightest claim on purpose.

briefing.mission: Know what you already are: salt that keeps its taste, light that was never meant to hide.

points.p: The Beatitudes flip the scoreboard before the chapter asks for anything: the poor in spirit, the mourners, the meek: blessed first, assigned second.
Flavor and preservation. The warning isn't about failing. It's about going bland and calling it blending in.
Visibility is the design, not the accident. Let the light land where people see it, and let the credit travel up, not out.
Six times the chapter takes the law deeper: anger, honesty, retaliation, enemies. The standard moves from the hands to the heart.

questions: Where have you dimmed on purpose, and who taught you to?
Salt works by contact. Where does your life actually touch people who taste the difference?
Which 'but I tell you' lands hardest on you right now?
briefing.prayer: God, keep the taste in me. Set my light where You want it seen, and let the glory travel past me to You. Amen.

drops.line: The field set. Sent out sharp and clean, both at once.
drops.why: Matthew 10 is marching orders: go, travel light, be shrewd without losing your innocence. Olive drab because the mission is real.

briefing.mission: Marching orders: go light, go wise, go anyway.

points.p: The twelve get named before they get sent. Identity precedes assignment: you're a person on the roster, not a number in a crowd.
No gold, no bag, no second coat. The mission funds the mission, and everything you'd over-pack is weight the road doesn't need.
The line on the back of the set: shrewd and clean at the same time. Neither cancels the other: wisdom without edge, innocence without naivety.
Fear gets answered with worth: not one sparrow falls unnoticed, and you are counted down to the hair. Courage here is arithmetic, not bravado.

questions: What would 'travel light' have you put down this season?
Where do you need more serpent, and where more dove?
What's the assignment you keep waiting to feel ready for?
briefing.prayer: Lord, send me sharp and keep me clean. Give me wisdom that doesn't harden and innocence that doesn't fold. I'll go. Amen.

benched.line: The closer. The season ends where the book does: with a sending.
benched.why: Matthew 28 is the Great Commission: all authority, then go. The lightest colorway closes the season the way the resurrection closes the Gospel: walking out in daylight.

briefing.mission: The tomb is open and the credential is signed. Go make disciples.

points.p: The women get the news first and running becomes the right response. The season's lightest colorway starts at a grave that didn't hold.
The commission opens with the credential, not the command. 'All authority in heaven and on earth' is the backing on every assignment that follows.
The assignment is reproduction: disciples who make disciples. Not an audience. A lineage.
The book closes on presence, not pressure: 'I am with you always, even to the end of the age.' The walk is accompanied.

questions: If the authority is His, what exactly are you still waiting to be qualified for?
Who taught you, and who are you teaching?
Where does 'with you always' need to land in your week?
briefing.prayer: Jesus, You hold the authority and I hold the assignment. Walk with me all the days. I'll walk in purpose. Amen.
